note: The Gambia: nationals of the African Union's, the Commonwealth's, the EU's and EFTA's states and of the others listed enter without a visa for 90 days; US citizens get a 30-day visa on arrival; everyone else needs a visa from a Gambian mission (or on arrival at Banjul where there's none in their country, not modelled). The USD 20 security fee each way isn't modelled. Read from Wikipedia's copy of the Tourism Board's list and Timatic. Read on 2026-11-03 against the Gambia Immigration Department's own visa page: it gives free entry only to the ECOWAS states (Mauritania, Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso 'privileges as accorded') and 18 countries with visa exemption agreements, and sorts everyone else into those needing a visa, an entry clearance or both, the United States among those needing a visa; but it still names the Netherlands Antilles (dissolved in 2010), Swaziland beside Eswatini, and places such as Flores, Lombok and Tasmania as countries, warns that its statuses 'are subjected to changes', and is undated, so it is recorded here and not held. The lead should weigh it against Wikipedia's copy, on which every figure stands.
